question: The recent detection of cases of African swine fever (ASF) in Catalonia has resulted in farreaching consequences for trade despite the fact that the outbreak is confined exclusively to wildlife and that there have been no cases in pig farms. The Spanish government has preventively blocked around 120 health certificates for export to around 40 countries.

This situation creates a significant economic risk for a sector, the exports of which are worth approximately EUR 8 800 million a year, and highlights the need for coordinated action at European level to ensure that localised outbreaks, which are fully controlled in accordance with EU rules, do not result in disproportionate trade restrictions by partners outside the EU. In light of the above: 1.

What actions is the Commission taking alongside the Spanish Government to prevent disproportionate restrictions on imports of Spanish pork, such as updating the guidelines on health regionalisation to prevent unjustified barriers in foreign markets?

Does the Commission intend to grant exceptional aid to the pigmeat market under Article 219 of the common market organisation regulation to cushion the economic impact of the outbreak on exports, which constitute one of the main pillars of the Spanish sector?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) 1. The EU has established rules to prevent the spread of African swine fever within an affected Member State, focusing on regionalisation as outlined in both the African swine fever EU guidelines1 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/5942.

These guidelines are rooted in scientific principles and aligned with international standards set by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). The Commission has actively pursued various actions in both bilateral and multilateral fora, such as the World Trade Organization (WTO).

Its aim is to address potential unjustified refusals by any third countries and to ensure that third countries acknowledge the EU’s approach based on a regionalisation of measures addressing outbreaks of African swine fever. The goal is to ensure adherence to international standards and protect the interests of affected Member States.

The Commission remains committed to ongoing diplomatic and technical dialogue with countries enforcing any bans in this respect, advocating for the recognition of the regionalisation approach and showcasing the effectiveness of the control measures implemented. 2.

The Commission is closely monitoring developments in the pigmeat sector and will act in a responsible and proportionate manner, within the limits of the legal framework and available budgetary resources, should circumstances so require.
1 Commission Notice on the guidelines on the prevention, control and eradication of African swine fever in the

Union (ASF guidelines), C/2023/7855, OJ C, C/2023/1504, 18.12.2023 ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/C/2023/1504/oj. 2 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/594 of 16 March 2023 laying down special disease control measures for African swine fever and repealing Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/605 (OJ L 79, 17.3.2023, p. 65, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2023/594/oj).
